items.title: Muslim Community Center Of Tucson
items.summary: This lecture discusses the Prophet Muhammad's descriptions of the Antichrist (Dajjal), including his 40-day presence on earth, his rapid movement across lands, his miraculous abilities, and his encounter with a young man. The speaker explains how these accounts should be understood literally based on Islamic jurisprudence regarding prayer during this period.

items.title: Muslim Community Center Of Tucson
items.aiTitle: Types of Filth in Islamic Purification Law
items.summary: A detailed discussion of the various categories of filth (najasah) as outlined in Islamic jurisprudence, including human waste, animal secretions, and related rulings on purity. The lecture covers specific substances and their classifications within the framework of Islamic law on purification.

items.title: Muslim Community Center Of Tucson
items.aiTitle: The Dajjal's Emergence and Duration: Hadith Analysis
items.summary: A detailed examination of a lengthy hadith narration recorded by Muslim regarding the Dajjal (false messiah), focusing on his emergence between Al and Hashem, his 40-day reign with manipulated time periods, and the gradual loss of his power. The lecture explores the literal interpretation of these events and their implications for Islamic belief and practice.

items.title: Muslim Community Center Of Tucson
items.aiTitle: Purification in Islam: Types of Filth and Ritual Purity
items.summary: A detailed discussion of the Islamic jurisprudence of purification, covering various types of filth and bodily discharges, with emphasis on the ruling regarding pre-seminal fluid (madhī) and the importance of seeking knowledge. The lecture includes a hadith about a companion's struggle with this issue and the Prophet's clarification that only washing is required, illustrating how knowledge relieves hardship.

items.title: Muslim Community Center Of Tucson
items.aiTitle: Pre-Islamic Superstitions and the Prophet's Teachings
items.summary: This lecture discusses pre-Islamic Arabian superstitions, including fortune-telling through lots at the Kaaba and beliefs about unlucky times and animals, explaining how the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) eradicated these false beliefs from the hearts of the Muslims through Islamic teachings.

items.title: Muslim Community Center Of Tucson
items.aiTitle: The Importance of Brotherhood and Community in Islam
items.summary: A lecture emphasizing the spiritual necessity of Muslim brotherhood and sisterhood, using Quranic verses and Prophetic traditions to illustrate how believers need one another to achieve paradise. The speaker discusses the analogy of believers as a unified building and references the Battle of Badr to demonstrate principles of community and obedience.

items.title: Muslim Community Center Of Tucson
items.summary: This lecture discusses the Islamic legal definition of filth (najasah), specifically examining urine and feces as inherently filthy substances according to Quranic and Sunnah evidence. The instructor emphasizes the importance of understanding the scriptural basis for Islamic rulings rather than merely accepting them through cultural knowledge.

items.title: Muslim Community Center Of Tucson
items.aiTitle: Understanding Quranic Wealth: A Deep Look at Divine Provision
items.summary: This lecture examines a well-known Quranic verse about the Prophet Muhammad's material condition, exploring the distinction between physical poverty and spiritual wealth. The speaker explains how the Prophet's true legacy was not material possessions but the knowledge and guidance he transmitted to others.

items.title: Muslim Community Center Of Tucson
items.aiTitle: Types of Filth and Purification in Islamic Law
items.summary: This lecture discusses the Islamic legal classification of filth (najasah) according to the book of purification, categorizing different types of impurities into three levels of intensity and explaining the evidence from the Quran and Sunnah. The instructor covers human waste as the most commonly encountered filth and outlines the specific purification methods required for each category.

items.title: Muslim Community Center Of Tucson
items.summary: This lecture explores the Islamic legal concept of najasah (filth) from the book of purification, explaining the distinction between what is ritually impure versus what is merely forbidden. The instructor establishes foundational principles for identifying najasah based on Quranic and Sunnah sources, emphasizing that everything is presumed pure and permissible unless specifically designated otherwise.

items.title: Muslim Community Center Of Tucson
items.aiTitle: The Book of Purification: Types of Water in Islamic Law
items.summary: This lecture discusses the Islamic jurisprudential classification of water into pure and impure categories, using the example of a well near Medina to illustrate when water becomes unsuitable for ritual purification. The instructor explains the principle that water remains pure unless contaminated by filth that changes its color, taste, or smell, and addresses scholarly disagreements about whether diluted liquids like tea or coffee constitute a third category.

items.title: Muslim Community Center Of Tucson
items.aiTitle: The Quran's Living Dialogue and Signs of the Day of Judgment
items.summary: This lecture explores the Quran as a living, dynamic text that engages believers in dialogue with Allah, and discusses major signs of the Day of Judgment including the sun rising from the west and the emergence of the Dabbah (animal from the earth) that will distinguish believers from disbelievers.

items.title: Muslim Community Center Of Tucson
items.aiTitle: Al-Wajeez: Book of Purification - Water and Its Types
items.summary: A lecture on the opening chapter of Al-Wajeez covering the book of purification, focusing on the rulings regarding water as the primary means of ritual purification. The instructor explains the default state of water from natural sources and presents Quranic and prophetic evidence for the purity and purifying nature of water, including seawater.

items.title: Muslim Community Center Of Tucson
items.aiTitle: Surah Al-Yunus: Refutation of Disbelief and the Day of Judgment
items.summary: A detailed Quranic exegesis of Surah Al-Yunus, focusing on its comprehensive refutation of pre-Islamic beliefs and disbelief, and concluding with an explanation of the verse asking what disbelievers are waiting for—the angels of death, Allah's arrival, or the major signs of the Day of Judgment.

items.title: Muslim Community Center Of Tucson
items.aiTitle: Al-Wajeez: Beginning the Book of Purification
items.summary: This lecture marks the completion of the book of fasting in Al-Wajeez and the beginning of the book of purification. The instructor discusses how Islamic jurisprudence books are traditionally organized following the famous narration of Gabriel, starting with the pillars of Islam and purification as foundational topics.
